transferable_rules: Use a time-bound challenge hook that creates urgency immediately
Progress through micro-steps with frequent visual resets and fast montage pacing
Mix creator face, screen capture, product visuals, and environment shots
Use absurdist hyperbole and self-aware humor instead of polished corporate tone
End with a punchline tied back to the challenge constraint
Let audience curiosity drive implicit CTA and sequel demand

transferable_rules: Lead with a curiosity-heavy colloquial hook rather than product description
Use anti-patterns and expectation subversion to stand out from over-edited ads
Keep production simple when personality or novelty carries the scene
Use satire, deadpan delivery, memes, and internet-culture references
Prefer original audio/voice when it strengthens creator identity
Use proof cues and audience reaction without overexplaining
Keep CTA implicit when content naturally creates product curiosity

transferable_rules: Entertain before selling; make the ad feel like content
Lead with a bold capability promise tied directly to buyer intent
Use brand confidence and personality as part of the value proposition
Favor smooth, rewatchable editing over hard-sell product listing
Use humor and an unexpected payoff to create comments and shares
Keep the CTA implicit when brand recall and trust matter more than immediate click-through
Let audience comments reveal live purchase intent and product requests

products where brand personality materially affects trust

references.source: Instagram public Reel / browser-inspected caption, comments, and context
references.creator: @robertmckeaveney
transferable_rules: Continuously monitor short-form platforms for formats with proven engagement
Decompose each winner into hook, pacing, beat structure, visual resets, humor device, proof cue, and CTA
Rebuild the format around a different product, script, footage, examples, and brand voice
Prefer proven structural patterns over inventing every format from zero
Move fast while the format is still culturally relevant
Measure the variation against the source pattern on retention and engagement, not visual similarity
originality_guardrails: Do not reuse creator identity or likeness
Do not copy exact scenes, proprietary footage, logos, or music without rights
Do not present another creator's results as CYZOR results

references.source: Instagram public Reel / browser-inspected caption, comments, thumbnails, and context
references.creator: @almu_yousef
transferable_rules: Use a curiosity-first caption that withholds explanation until the visual payoff
Structure the demo as setup → action → impressive result → abrupt confident close
Make the output/result the hero instead of narrating every feature
Use cursor movement, zoom-ins, split-screen, or before/after framing to guide attention
Favor simple direct cuts and fast 2-4 second visual beats over decorative transitions
Design the demo to naturally trigger useful questions rather than forced engagement bait
Use original audio, screen audio, voiceover, or silence intentionally; do not add music that obscures the demo
End immediately after the payoff to increase loopability
Use verifiable proof such as working output, source/repo/product page, or measured result
Target a need-to-know audience whose engagement quality matters more than broad reach
originality_guardrails: Do not fake community comments or pretend a planted commenter is independent proof
Do not fabricate product outputs or before/after results
Do not reuse exact creator dialogue, footage, or proprietary assets

transferable_grammar.focal_density: one primary action plus at most one supporting prop/text cluster
transferable_grammar.motion: pose change or prop movement at each beat; avoid static lecture framing
transferable_grammar.accent_color: limited high-contrast accent for the active concept

ecommerce_trending_style.pacing: choose either rapid 2-4 second progression or deliberate anti-pattern slow/no-cut delivery when the joke depends on it
ecommerce_trending_style.visual_mix: creator face + screen capture + product + environment + meme/screenshot inserts
ecommerce_trending_style.humor: deadpan, absurdist hyperbole, self-awareness, expectation subversion
ecommerce_trending_style.proof: visible product demo, audience reactions, comments, build progress, results only when verified
ecommerce_trending_style.cta: implicit curiosity-driven CTA first; direct CTA only when the buying path is frictionless
ecommerce_trending_style.adaptation_rule: borrow pacing, narrative devices, and editing grammar; never copy exact dialogue, characters, or scenes

entertainment_first_product_promo.structure: setup → confident solution → humorous or unexpected payoff
entertainment_first_product_promo.editing: smooth, polished, highly rewatchable; product/service remains legible
entertainment_first_product_promo.humor: self-aware confidence, meme-ready punchline, no forced corporate tone
entertainment_first_product_promo.proof: inventory/service capability, audience reactions, real buyer comments, verified results only
entertainment_first_product_promo.cta: implicit brand-recall CTA by default; direct CTA only when frictionless and natural
entertainment_first_product_promo.ideal_use: high-ticket, local, service-heavy, or personality-led products

workflow: QA for originality, clarity, and retention
publish only when publication is enabled
compare performance and keep winning variants
viral_format_replication.selection_rule: Prioritize recent formats with strong engagement, clear audience-product fit, and repeatable structure.
viral_format_replication.adaptation_rule: Replicate mechanics and pacing, not protected expression or exact creative.
viral_format_replication.speed_rule: Use proven formats while they are still current; archive stale patterns.

product_demo_short_form.pacing: 2-4 second visual beats; use faster cuts only when clarity remains high
product_demo_short_form.framing: show-dont-tell; product output is the hero
product_demo_short_form.guidance: cursor path, zoom, split-screen, before/after, callouts only where needed
product_demo_short_form.proof: real working output, verified numbers, authentic customer evidence, or direct demonstration
product_demo_short_form.cta: implicit curiosity first; direct CTA only when buying path and claims are verified
product_demo_short_form.loop: end on the payoff or a visual state that makes the opening feel natural on replay
